newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-RAIDERS DEFENSIVE END PAT SWILLING RETIRES.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-RAIDERS DEFENSIVE END PAT SWILLING RETIRES.

text.p: Oakland Raiders defensive end Pat Swilling, who has been bothered by a pulled stomach muscle in the preseason, announced his retirement Saturday.

Swilling originally announced his retirement when he walked out of training camp in late July, but returned three days later. But this time it appears the retirement is real, although Swilling did not make himself available to the media before Oakland's preseason game Saturday against New Orleans.

The 32-year-old Swilling, one of the NFL's premier pass rushers and a one-time Defensive Player of the Year, had become strictly a pass-rushing specialist for the Raiders. With first-round pick Darrell Russell, Lance Johnstone and Anthony Smith at the ends, Swilling's playing time figured to be severely curtailed.
Swilling ranked second in the NFL with 13 sacks in his first year with the Raiders in 1995. He had six sacks last season.

Swilling was named to the Pro Bowl five times in his 11-year career. He was named NFL Defensive Player of the Year in 1989 when he had 16 1/2 sacks for the New Orleans Saints. Swilling led the NFL with 17 sacks in 1991.

After playing seven years for the Saints, Swilling was traded to the Detroit Lions on draft day of 1993. He spent two years with the Lions before he signed as an unrestricted free agent with Oakland in April of 1995.
